title: Billie Holiday's voice and character
summary: Edison and Dance discuss her early and late voice, and he praises her as a woman who gave herself completely to the men she loved.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: When you come to originators in sounds, nobody sounds like Lady Day.

Well, you know, they just reissued everything she did, major. Columbia just put out an album she made, an album of things that were really the second rate, you know, from the early days. The least good. They're okay, they're not bad. But it's very interesting. The thing, you know -- I heard her when she first started, and I didn't like the Lady, yes, when the voice started thickening --
The quality was gone, oh, yeah.

And, you know, a lot of people seem to me to like that. It's kind of a morbid thing, Almost reveling in the dying hours, I think. But when I was playing this record I realized what it was, you know, the early ones she sounds like a girl. The later ones she sounds sort of like a --

Yeah. Her voice had almost gone. I just really loved her. I think she was just absolutely fantastic. Good woman, good heart. She was just -- she was a victim of love, because she loved everybody that she ever was affiliated with, you know.
She had some pretty bad-luck with those guys, didn't she.
She loved them. She had complete confidence in everybody she was with, sure. She turned her complete life over to them. Career, everything. When she started going with a man, she gave him everything.
